clue.text: Could be either I or Adam!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pronoun of the speaker
second meaning: in Genesis the first human ever made

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what one label could fit both a single letter and the biblical first man.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are grammatical (the speaker's pronoun) and literal (the earliest human in the Bible).
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the speaker's pronoun this way, and the Bible makes Adam the earliest human, so the phrase fits both.

clue.text: They're not who they claim to be–the little devil so "up," what's left is a mess!

definitions.text: They're not who they claim to be

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word so is written bottom to top

parts.note: the little word so is taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: is a mess marks the letters of the word for what's left as scrambled

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Exposing fakes, with a mischievous sprite hoisted up and leaving chaos behind.
explanation.walkthrough: This spelling with -ERS is a recognised variant of the -ORS form.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is a fraud who pretends to be someone else, so such people are not who they claim.

clue.text: Say about what might be found in the velvet glove, turned to give enough.

indicators.note: say about means the word say goes around the rest

parts.note: the word say is taken as written and wraps the rest

indicators.note: turned means the letters of the hand word are churned into a new order

parts.words: what might be found in the velvet glove
parts.note: the idiom an iron fist in a velvet glove: firmness under gentle manners

explanation.surface: Talk of the hard fist hidden inside gentle manners, turned to good use.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a need is to meet it in full, providing as much as is needed.

clue.text: Carefully examine the twisted rope!

indicators.note: a twisted rope is wound round itself, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word rope supplies its own four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a coil of rope closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over something is to study it closely and attentively.

clue.text: The man who takes things back (rats! one-fourth gone!) gives an account.

parts.words: The man who takes things back
parts.note: a repo man repossesses goods when payments stop; repo is the short name

indicators.note: one of the four letters of the word rats drops out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A repossession agent curses and then tells his story.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats is the exclamation; losing one of its four letters, the A, leaves three.
explanation.definitionFit: To report is to describe events or give a statement about what happened.

clue.text: " Well, well, well," says a well-known director!

definitions.text: " Well, well, well," says a well-known director!

parts.note: a run of wells, suggesting the surname Welles
the famous filmmaker whose surname sounds like wells; the answer is his first name

explanation.walkthrough: Orson Welles, who made Citizen Kane, has a surname that sounds like a string of wells.
explanation.definitionFit: This first name belongs to the Citizen Kane filmmaker, whose surname echoes the repeated word.

clue.text: Obviously, Rambo got arthritis in South America!

definitions.note: the definition is a place found in that continent rather than a plain noun

indicators.note: obviously hints that the answer is plain to see, sitting in the words that follow

parts.note: the city runs across the end of Rambo, all of got and the start of arthritis

explanation.surface: An action hero develops sore joints while abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia, a country of South America.

clue.text: One of those found at the banks is let up on the French capital of Rouen.

definitions.text: One of those found at the banks

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word let reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, here of the city name

parts.note: the French city whose initial supplies the last letter

explanation.surface: Something allowed upward on the French capital of Normandy, as if a travel note.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks suggests a river; it means the money kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller is the cashier who serves customers at a bank counter.

clue.text: Placed in one which should be really progressive, but I'm using it right now!

indicators.note: placed in tells us the word for placed goes inside the word for the promising one

parts.words: one which should be really progressive
parts.note: a comer is someone or something promising, expected to make real progress
put means placed or set down

explanation.surface: A musing on progress that ends with the setter pointing at the machine on the desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is typing the clue, so the definition points at the device in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter wrote the clue at a keyboard, so the device being used at that moment is this machine.

clue.text: Didn't bid with what you hear if over.

indicators.note: what you hear tells us the answer is how the word for over sounds when spoken

parts.note: past means over, finished, as in the danger is past

explanation.surface: A bridge player's turn described in a tangle of conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, saying pass instead of bidding is the usual call, so a player who didn't bid passed.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as bridge, a player who declines to make a bid is said to pass.

clue.text: To be made up of what is continued shortly about a diminutive nun.

indicators.note: about means the short form of continued goes around the little nun

parts.note: cont. is the usual short form of continued
a nun is a sister, and sis is the pet form of sister

explanation.surface: Something being composed of a serial story wrapped around a tiny nun, which is nonsense on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To consist of something is to be composed of it, made up of those parts.

clue.text: In an outstanding way, sort of angry about couple of numbers from old Rome.

indicators.note: about means the rearranged angry goes round the two Roman numerals
sort of means a version of the word angry, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the word angry supplies its own letters to be rearranged

parts.words: couple of numbers from old Rome
parts.note: D is 500 and L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone splendidly worked up over a pair of ancient Roman figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandly means in a splendid, impressive manner, which is an outstanding way of doing something.

clue.text: Run water over a nervous siren!

indicators.note: a nervous thing is jittery, so the letters of the word siren shift about

parts.note: the word siren supplies its own letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Splashing a jumpy sea-nymph with water to calm her.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to wash it lightly under running water.

clue.text: Rolls here, for example.

parts.note: on the surface a Rolls-Royce car; really bread rolls
the place where such things are made and sold

explanation.walkthrough: Rolls with its capital letter suggests the luxury car and a showroom; the rolls are bread, baked and sold in this shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or workplace where bread, rolls and cakes are baked and sold is called by this name.

clue.text: It's an awful sin to take such wild rides, but such should be pretty hip, usually!

definitions.text: such should be pretty hip, usually

indicators.note: awful marks the word sin as being in a mess, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the word sin supplies its own letters

indicators.note: wild marks the word rides as unruly, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the word rides supplies its own letters

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about reckless thrill rides, with a nod to how trendy their riders think they are.
explanation.definitionFit: People on the inside of a group are in the know, which is what being hip means.

clue.text: Degeneracy starts this month on a study on the Common Era.

parts.note: the puzzle appeared in December, abbreviated Dec
taken as written
a den is a private room for work, a study
CE stands for Common Era, the secular equivalent of AD

explanation.surface: Moral decline beginning this month, with an essay on the current era.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle was published in December, which makes this month Dec. CE stands for Common Era, the secular form of AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral or cultural decline, a falling off in standards.

clue.text: Serf's hen, twitchy, brightens things up.

indicators.note: a twitchy thing jerks about, so the letters of the serf's hen are jumbled

parts.note: the words serf's hen supply their own eight letters

explanation.surface: A peasant's nervous chicken livens up the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: To freshen things is to make them brighter and livelier, giving a cleaner new look.

clue.text: The door opened up around E.T., dizzy and unable to move.

indicators.note: around means the reworked door goes round the alien's initials
a door opened up is broken apart, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the word door supplies its own letters

indicators.note: dizzy means the two letters of E.T. are spun round

parts.note: E.T. is the title alien of the Spielberg film, giving his two initials

explanation.surface: The film alien, giddy and stuck as a door swings open around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rooted to the spot is fixed in place, as if planted in the ground.

clue.text: Grab 'em! O, chaos! There's no entrance or exit with it.

definitions.text: There's no entrance or exit with it

indicators.note: chaos signals disorder, so the letters of grab 'em O are jumbled

parts.note: the words grab 'em and O supply their own seven letters

explanation.surface: A cry to seize people amid uproar, with talk of no way in or out.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade, letting no goods in or out of a country.

clue.text: A large number to put on a show with you and me, but it's bound to have its sticking points!

definitions.text: it's bound to have its sticking points

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
to act is to perform, putting on a show
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: Staging a big production together, while warning that the project will hit snags.
explanation.walkthrough: Sticking points sound like disagreements; here they are the plant's literal prickles.
explanation.definitionFit: This desert plant is covered in spines, points that stick into anyone who touches it.

clue.text: Great! Cal eats Middle Eastern bread.

indicators.note: Cal eats means the name surrounds the bread, taking it inside

parts.note: taken as written
pita is a flat pocket bread from the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone named Cal tucks into flatbread and declares it great.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital! is an old-fashioned exclamation of approval meaning excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Sounds imaginary, but the kite flier and the projectionist do it.

definitions.text: the kite flier and the projectionist do it

indicators.note: sounds means the answer is spoken the same as the word for imaginary

parts.note: unreal means imaginary, not real

explanation.surface: An apparently fanciful comparison of a kite flier and a cinema projectionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite flier lets out string from a spool and a projectionist runs film off a spool, both unwinding.

clue.text: Scans around what would be great, in modern terms, and talks too!

indicators.note: around tells us the word for scans is placed round the slang for great

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over, an older sense close to scanning a page

parts.words: what would be great, in modern terms
parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, is modern slang for great

explanation.surface: Someone skims material for anything impressive and chats about it as well.
explanation.walkthrough: To con a text is an old verb for learning it by careful reading, which is the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Confabs is informal for chats or discussions, from confabulation, an old word for conversation.

clue.text: If you don't succeed, adding fifty will only cause you to thrash about.

indicators.note: adding means the Roman fifty is slipped into the word

parts.note: if you don't succeed, you fail
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb about trying again: failure leads only to helpless struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the saying if at first you don't succeed, try, try again.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail is to wave the arms or body about wildly and without control.

clue.text: Not Miss Muffet's favorites!

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme girl was frightened away from her tuffet
understatement: the creatures she would least like to see

explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Little Miss Muffet sat eating curds and whey until one of these sat down beside her and frightened her away.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's eight-legged visitor scared the girl off, so this creature is hardly her best-loved thing.

clue.text: Boast is a common start to a quarrel.

definitions.text: a common start to a quarrel
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in the idiom I have a ... to pluck with you, the ... is the grievance that opens a dispute

explanation.walkthrough: The old saying a crow to pluck (or pick) with someone means a grievance to settle, the opening of a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowing is bragging loudly, and a crow to pluck is an old idiom for a grievance to air.

clue.text: Put two and two together again, to fix things up!

parts.note: re- at the front of a word means again
to pair is to put things together in twos

explanation.surface: Advice to work something out a second time in order to set it right.
explanation.walkthrough: Put two and two together usually means to deduce; here it means to match things in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it, putting it back into working order.

clue.text: Tenure is, perhaps, with lots of followers.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version of the words tenure is, their letters rearranged

parts.note: the words tenure is supply their own eight letters

explanation.surface: An office holder's term in post comes with a large entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who accompany an important person, so several of them make many followers.

clue.text: He directs customers, but the insomniac might be one, too.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a department-store employee who guides shoppers around the sales floor

definitions.text: the insomniac might be one, too
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who cannot sleep paces the floor at night

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a job title in a large shop; the second is the sleepless person pacing back and forth across the room at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a shop attendant who supervises a sales floor, and also literally one who walks the floor.
